page: Amazon Web Services r6g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance features 64 dedicated physical cores from custom AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 512 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8 GB of RAM per core. The server includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes, and features a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps. Hardware acceleration via dedicated GPUs is not present.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput in parallelized and memory-centric workloads. The instance achieves strong results in stress-ng multi-core execution (97,058.58), small-block cached memory bandwidth (3,778.88 GB/sec), static web serving (45.29 GB/sec), and Clang software compilation (43,148.0). Redis SET operations also perform strongly at 77.23 million operations per second. Conversely, single-thread metrics reflect architectural tradeoffs: single-core Geekbench scores (974.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (20.33 GB/sec) rank in the lower quartile, and large-model LLM generation speeds remain weak due to the absence of matrix coprocessors or discrete accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture provides high density and operational efficiency across heavily parallel tasks compared to traditional architectures. With 64 unshared physical cores and large RAM capacity, r6g.16xlarge delivers consistent execution for concurrent services. This server profile is well matched for in-memory databases such as Redis and Memcached, high-concurrency caching tiers, large-scale distributed compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, and enterprise memory-bound data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r6g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 ARM cores running at 2.5 GHz and 512 GB of memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Operating on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong parallel throughput, highlighted by 77.23 million Redis SET operations per second, high Clang compilation scores, and robust multi-core stress execution. However, single-threaded processing and LLM text generation reflect lower relative efficiency. The hardware configuration delivers steady performance and cost-effective scaling for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory caches, distributed build pipelines, relational databases, and high-concurrency web serving.
